issues.description: The PersonService.getAllPersons method signature differs between the template/problem specification and the solution. The template (and the problem statement Part 3) expects a single-parameter method getAllPersons(PersonSortingOptions sortingOptions). In the solution repository PersonService the method was changed to getAllPersons(PersonSortingOptions sortingOptions, boolean includeInactive). However, the solution's PersonResource still calls personService.getAllPersons(new PersonSortingOptions(...)) with only one argument. This creates a compile-time mismatch and is structurally inconsistent: students following the problem/template will implement a single-parameter method, but the provided solution uses a different signature (and the solution itself contains an internal inconsistency between resource and service). This will confuse students and prevent straightforward comparison with the reference implementation.
issues.suggested_fix: Restore a consistent single-parameter API: change the solution's PersonService method back to public List<Person> getAllPersons(PersonSortingOptions sortingOptions) and implement the sorting logic there (or alternatively add an overloaded single-parameter method delegating to the two-parameter one). Ensure PersonResource calls the matching single-parameter method. If the extra boolean parameter is required for intended functionality, update the problem statement and the template to document and expose that parameter consistently, and update PersonResource to pass it.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect a server-side method PersonService.getAllPersons(PersonSortingOptions) (single parameter) to implement sorting (Part 3). In the solution repository, PersonService defines getAllPersons(PersonSortingOptions, boolean) (two parameters) instead. Meanwhile PersonResource in the solution calls personService.getAllPersons(new PersonSortingOptions(...)) with a single argument. This creates an inconsistency between the documented requirement, the template, and the solution: students will expect and implement a single-argument getAllPersons method (as instructed by the problem and template) but the solution's service method signature differs, which breaks the clear mapping from requirement -> resource -> service and can cause compilation/mapping confusion.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the service method signature consistent with the problem statement and template. Restore or add a single-argument method: public List<Person> getAllPersons(PersonSortingOptions sortingOptions) that implements the required sorting. If the two-argument variant (with boolean includeInactive) is needed, provide an overloaded single-argument method that delegates to it (e.g., getAllPersons(sortingOptions) -> return getAllPersons(sortingOptions, /*default*/ false)), and ensure PersonResource calls the single-argument method. This keeps the API consistent and preserves the intended student mapping from endpoints to service implementation.
